fact_tl: Noong 1876, naimbento ni Alexander Graham Bell ang telepono! Binabago nito ang boses mo sa signal sa kawad para makausap ang malalayong tao.
fact_en: In 1876, Alexander Graham Bell invented the telephone! It turns your voice into a signal through a wire to talk to people far away.

title: Ibon Flap vs Eroplano Engine
fact_tl: Pumapagaspas ang ibon para sa angat at sulong nang sabay! Ang eroplano ay may nakapirming pakpak at makina, kaya hindi na kailangang pumagaspas.
fact_en: Birds flap to get lift and forward push together! Airplanes have fixed wings for lift and engines for pushing, so they never need to flap.

title: Light Reactions vs Calvin Cycle
fact_tl: May dalawang bahagi ang photosynthesis! Una, sa light reactions, sumasalo ang halaman ng light, gumagawa ng energy molecules, at naglalabas ng oxygen. Pangalawa, sa Calvin cycle, ginagawa nila ang sugar mula sa carbon dioxide.
fact_en: Photosynthesis happens in two stages! First, in the light reactions, plants capture light, make energy molecules, and release oxygen. Second, in the Calvin cycle, they build sugar from carbon dioxide.

title: Jeepney 60 Kilometro 2 Oras 30
fact_tl: Kung umabot ang jeep ng 60 kilometro sa bayan sa loob ng 2 oras, ang average speed nito ay 30 km/h! Totoo ito kahit tumigil sa trapiko o bumilis.
fact_en: If a jeepney travels 60 kilometers to town in 2 hours, its average speed is 30 km/h! This is true even if it stopped in traffic or sped up.

title: Stop Trapsik Oras Kasama Average
fact_tl:
Nakakaapekto ba ang pagpahinga o pagkaharang sa trapiko sa iyong average speed?

Oo! Kasama pa rin ang oras na iyon. Kaya ang average speed ay mas mababa kaysa sa pinakamabilis mong takbo!
fact_en:
Does resting or getting stuck in traffic affect your average speed?

Yes! That stopped time still counts. That's why your average speed is usually lower than your absolute fastest running pace!

title: Average Speed Hindi Gitna Numero
fact_tl:
Ang average speed mo ba ay yung nasa gitna ng pinakamabilis at pinakamabagal mong bilis?

Hindi! Kung magkaiba ang oras, mali iyon. Ang tamang average speed ay laging kabuuang layo na hinati sa kabuuang oras!
fact_en:
Is your average speed just the middle number between your fastest and slowest speeds?

Nope! If the times differ, that's wrong. The real average speed is always your total distance divided by your total time!

title: Formula Distansya Oras Hanapin
fact_tl:
Paano mo malalaman ang layo o oras kung alam mo na ang average speed mo?

I-rearrange lang ang formula! I-multiply ang speed sa time para makuha ang distance, o hatiin ang distance sa speed. Halimbawa, 5 m/s sa 10 segundo ay 50 metro!
fact_en:
How can you find distance or time if you already know your average speed?

Just rearrange the formula! Multiply speed by time for distance, or divide distance by speed for time. For example, 5 m/s for 10 seconds is 50 meters!

title: 400 Metro Oval 80 Segundo 5
fact_tl:
Kung tumakbo ka ng 400-metro na oval sa loob ng 80 segundo, ano ang average speed mo?

Ito ay 5 meters per second! Hatiin mo lang ang 400 metro sa 80 segundo. Ito ang average speed mo, kahit pumabilis at bumagal ka habang tumatakbo!
fact_en:
If you run a 400-meter oval in 80 seconds, what is your average speed?

It's 5 meters per second! You just divide the 400 meters by 80 seconds. This is your average speed, even if you sped up and slowed down while running!

title: Average kumpara Constant Speed
fact_tl:
Laging pareho ba ang average speed sa totoong bilis mo?

Hindi laging pareho! Kung constant ang takbo mo, ang average speed ay katumbas niyon. Kung bumibilis at bumabagal ka, ang average speed ay nasa pagitan ng pinakamabilis at pinakamabagal.
fact_en:
Is average speed always the same as your actual speed?

Not always! If you move at a constant speed the whole time, average speed equals it exactly. But if you speed up and slow down, average speed falls between your fastest and slowest.

title: Bagay Bilis Lakad Sasakyan Iba
fact_tl:
Gaano kabilis ang iba't ibang bagay?

Napakakaiba-iba! Ang naglalakad ay 4 km/h, ang sasakyan sa highway ay 80 km/h, at ang eroplano ay umaabot ng 900 km/h. Ang average speed ay nakakatulong sa pagkumpara.
fact_en:
How fast do different things move?

Very differently! A walking person goes about 4 km/h, a highway car about 80 km/h, and a passenger plane reaches about 900 km/h. Average speed helps us compare them.

title: Bakit Hati Distansya Oras Bawat
fact_tl:
Bakit hinahati natin ang layo sa oras?

Para malaman kung gaano karaming layo ang nalalakbay sa BAWAT yunit ng oras! Hinati ang 100 metro sa 20 segundo, para malaman kung ilang metro ang natatapos kada segundo.
fact_en:
Why do we divide distance by time?

To find out how much distance is covered in EACH single unit of time! Dividing 100 meters by 20 seconds tells us how many meters are completed every second.

title: Coach Average Speed Atleta Track
fact_tl:
Paano nalalaman ng mga coach kung gumagaling ang atleta?

Ginagamit nila ang average speed! Kung mas mababa ang oras ng manlalaro sa parehong distansya, mas mataas ang average speed niya, na palatandaan ng pag-unlad.
fact_en:
How do coaches know if an athlete is getting better?

They use average speed! If a player's time drops over the same distance, their average speed is higher, which is a clear sign of progress.

title: Switch Bridge Circuit On Off
fact_tl:
Ano ang ginagawa ng switch?

Ito ay parang tulay sa loob ng circuit! Kapag naka-on, dinidikit nito ang daanan kaya umaagos ang current. Kapag naka-off, pinuputol nito ang daanan kaya tumitigil ang current.
fact_en:
What does a switch do?

It acts like a bridge inside the circuit! When it's on, it connects the path so current flows. When it's off, it breaks the path so the current stops.

title: Eroplano Bago Barko
fact_tl: Binago ng eroplano ang paglalakbay! Ang biyaheng dating tumatagal ng mga buwan sa barko ay nagagawa na sa ilang oras lang, kaya mas madaling makarating sa malalayong bansa.
fact_en: Airplanes changed travel! A trip that once took months by ship now takes just hours, making it easy to reach faraway countries.

title: Segundo lang, Balita sa Mundo
fact_tl:
Paano binago ng internet ang buhay?

Sa loob ng ilang segundo, makakahanap, makakapagpadala, at makakapagbahagi na tayo ng impormasyon, balita, larawan, at mensahe sa kahit sinong tao sa mundo!
fact_en:
How did the internet change life?

In just seconds, we can find, send, and share information, news, pictures, and messages with almost anyone in the world!

title: Bombilya Hindi Uubos Current
fact_tl:
Naubos ba ng bombilya ang current?

Hindi! Ang current na pumapasok sa bombilya ay kasing-dami ng lumalabas. Ang nauubos ay ang enerhiya, na nagiging liwanag at init—hindi ang current mismo!
fact_en:
Does the bulb 'use up' the current?

Nope! The current entering the bulb equals the current leaving. What actually gets used up is energy, turning into light and heat—not the current itself!

title: Voltage Push Current Daloy
fact_tl: Ang voltage ang 'push' na nagpapadaloy ng current, sinusukat sa volts. Ang current ang aktwal na dami, sinusukat sa amperes. Parang tubig: voltage ang presyon, current ang daloy!
fact_en: Voltage is the 'push' driving the current, measured in volts. Current is the actual amount flowing, measured in amperes. Like water: voltage is pressure, current is the flow!

title: Geothermal Balon Steam Turbine
fact_tl: Ang geothermal plant ay gumagamit ng malalalim na balon para kunin ang init! Ang singaw ay dumadaan sa mga tubo papunta sa turbine at generator para gumawa ng kuryente. Pagkatapos, ibinabalik ang tubig sa ilalim para magamit ulit!
fact_en: A geothermal plant uses deep wells to bring up heat! Steam travels through pipes to spin the turbine and generator, making electricity. Then the water goes back underground to be reused!

title: Tongonan Leyte Geothermal Field
fact_tl:
Saan sa Pilipinas makikita ang malaking geothermal field?

Sa Tongonan, Leyte, may malaking geothermal field na nagbibigay ng kuryente sa maraming bahay sa Visayas! Ito ay tunay na halimbawa kung paano ginagamit ng Pilipinas ang init ng lupa para sa kuryente.
fact_en:
Where in the Philippines can we find a big geothermal field?

In Tongonan, Leyte, there's a huge geothermal field that powers many homes across the Visayas! It's a real-life example of how the Philippines uses the Earth's heat for electricity.

title: Geothermal Gabi Tuloy
fact_tl:
Bakit ang geothermal energy ay gumagana kahit sa gabi?

Ang solar power ay nangangailangan ng sikat ng araw, kaya tumitigil ito sa gabi o kapag maulap. Pero ang geothermal ay gumagana araw at gabi dahil laging mainit sa ilalim ng lupa!
fact_en:
Why can geothermal energy work even at night?

Solar power needs sunlight, so it stops at night or when it's cloudy. But geothermal works day and night because it's always hot underground!

title: Geothermal Hindi Lava Singaw
fact_tl:
Kinukuha ba ng geothermal ang lava mismo mula sa ilalim?

Hindi! Hindi gumagamit ang geothermal ng totoong lava. Sa halip, ginagamit nito ang init na ipinapasa ng lupa sa tubig, na nagiging mainit na singaw—hindi totoong lava!
fact_en:
Does geothermal energy scoop up lava from underground?

Nope! Geothermal doesn't use actual lava. Instead, it uses the heat the ground passes into water, turning it into hot steam—not actual lava!

title: Malalim na Balon Kilometro Init
fact_tl: Para makahanap ng sapat na init, naghuhukay ang mga trabahador ng napakalalim na balon, ilang kilometro pababa! Napakainit doon kaya nagiging singaw ang tubig.
fact_en: To find enough heat, workers drill super deep wells, sometimes kilometers down! It’s so hot down there that it turns water right into steam.

title: Geothermal Tuloy-Tuloy Kuryente
fact_tl:
Bakit magandang pundasyon ang geothermal para sa kuryente natin?

Hindi tulad ng hangin o araw na minsan nawawala, ang geothermal ay nagbibigay ng tuloy-tuloy na kuryente buong araw!
fact_en:
Why is geothermal a strong base for our power supply?

Unlike wind or sun that sometimes stop, geothermal gives steady electricity all day long!

title: Geothermal Tubig Pananim Paligo
fact_tl: Bukod sa kuryente, ang init ng geothermal ay pwedeng magpainit ng tubig, magpatuyo ng pananim, o gumawa ng mainit na paliguan!
fact_en: Besides making electricity, geothermal heat can warm water, dry crops, or fill cozy warm baths! It’s not just for power.

title: Init Mundo Hindi Mauubos
fact_tl: Iniisip ng iba na nauubos ang init ng Mundo, pero napakalaki nito! Matagal pa itong mananatiling mainit, kaya hindi ito mauubos kung gagamitin nang tama.
fact_en: Some think Earth's heat runs out, but it's actually enormous! It stays hot for a very long time, so it won't run out if used wisely.

title: Geothermal Kuryente Bahay PH
fact_tl:
Saan natin ginagamit ang kuryente mula sa geothermal sa Pilipinas?

Nagbibigay-ilaw ito sa mga bahay, eskwelahan, at tindahan! Posibleng ang ilang gamit ninyo sa bahay ay pinapagana ng init ng lupa.
fact_en:
What do we use geothermal electricity for in the Philippines?

It lights up homes, schools, and shops! Some appliances in your house might actually be powered by the Earth's heat.

title: Bato Lupa Init Paa Hadlang
fact_tl: Bakit hindi natin nararamdaman ang init sa paa? Makapal na bato at lupa ang nasa pagitan natin at ng mainit na bahagi, kaya hindi umaabot ang init sa ibabaw!
fact_en: Why don't we feel the heat under our feet? Thick rock and soil sit between us and the hot part below, so the heat never reaches the surface!

title: Geothermal Walang Gasolina Coal
fact_tl: Ang geothermal ay kahanga-hanga — hindi kailangan ng gasolina o karbon! Ginagamit lang nito ang init na nakatago sa loob ng Daigdig, kaya hindi tayo umaasa sa angkat na panggatong.
fact_en: Geothermal power is amazing — it doesn't need gasoline or coal! It simply uses the heat already hiding inside the Earth, so we don't depend on imported fuel.

title: Ligtas Plant Malapit Bulkan
fact_tl:
Ligtas ba ang magtayo ng power plant malapit sa bulkan?

Oo! Pinag-aaralan ng mga inhinyero ang bulkan nang maigi, pinipili ang pinakaligtas na lugar, at lagi itong binabantayan — kaya ligtas itong gumana.
fact_en:
Is it safe to build a power plant near a volcano?

Yes! Engineers study the volcano carefully, pick the safest spots, and always monitor it — so the plant can operate safely without any danger.

title: Kiskis Ipon Charge ZAP Spark
fact_tl: Kapag nagkikiskisan ang dalawang bagay, maliliit na charge na tinatawag na electrons ay lumilipat sa isa. Nagtitipon ang sobrang charge hanggang—ZAP!—biglang tatalon ito sa ibang bagay. Iyon ang spark!
fact_en: When two things rub together, tiny charges called electrons move from one to the other. The extra charge piles up until—ZAP!—it jumps across to another object. That jump is the spark!

title: Mabagal Ipon Biglang Labas
fact_tl:
Bakit parang biglaan ang static spark?

May dalawang bahagi ang static spark! Una, dahan-dahang nagtitipon ang charge habang naglalakad ka o nagkikiskis ang damit. Pangalawa, bigla itong lumalabas. Matagal ang ipon, pero sandali lang ang labas!
fact_en:
Why does a static spark feel so sudden?

A static spark has two stages! First, charge slowly builds up while you walk or clothes rub. Second, it rushes out in a flash. Storing takes time, but release is instant!

title: Doorknob Shock sa Tuyong Panahon
fact_tl: Kapag naglalakad sa carpet na may tsinelas, nagtitipon ang charge! Hawakan ang metal doorknob, at lalaktaw ang charge para sa maliit na zap. Madalas ito kapag tuyo ang panahon.
fact_en: Walking on a carpet in slippers builds up charge! Touch a metal doorknob, and the charge jumps for a tiny zap. This happens most when the weather is dry.

title: Humid na Pilipinas Walang Spark
fact_tl:
Bakit bihira tayong makaramdam ng static spark sa Pilipinas?

Madalas mahalumigmig ang ating hangin at puno ng tubig! Tumutulong ito para dahan-dahang umalis ang sobrang charge. Kaya mas madalas ang static spark sa air-conditioned na kwarto o kapag tuyo.
fact_en:
Why do we rarely feel a static spark in the Philippines?

Our air is often humid and full of water! This helps extra charge leak away slowly. That is why static sparks happen more in an air-conditioned room or dry weather.

title: Hindi Delikadong Static Shock
fact_tl: Akala mo delikado ang static spark sa doorknob? Hindi ito nakakasama! Napakaliit lang ng charge, kaya nakakagulat lang ito. Iba ito sa delikadong kuryente sa wall socket na hindi dapat hawakan.
fact_en: Think a doorknob static spark is dangerous? It cannot hurt you! The charge is very small, just surprising you. This differs from dangerous wall socket electricity you must never touch.

title: Gas Station sa Static Spark
fact_tl:
Bakit may babala tungkol sa static spark sa gasolinahan?

Ang singaw ng gasolina ay madaling masunog, kaya kahit maliit na spark ay pwedeng magsimula ng apoy! Kaya minsan hinihipo muna ng tao ang metal ng kotse para mawala ang charge bago humawak sa gasolina.
fact_en:
Why are there warnings about static sparks at a gas station?

Gasoline vapor catches fire easily, so a tiny spark can start a flame! That is why you should touch the car's metal first to drain your charge before handling the fuel.

title: Positive Negative Charge Dalawa
fact_tl: May dalawang uri ng charge: positibo at negatibo! Kung sobra ang negatibo sa isang bagay at kulang sa kabila, gusto nilang magbalanse. Ang spark ay nangyayari kapag ang sobrang charge ay tumalon, para bumalik sa balanse.
fact_en: There are two charges: positive and negative! If one object has too much negative and another too little, they want to balance. The spark happens when extra charge jumps, returning both to balance.

title: Spark Lundoon Malapad na Gap
fact_tl:
Kaya ba tumalon ang spark sa malawak na puwang ng hangin?

Oo! Mas malaking electric charge ang gumagawa ng mas mataas na voltage, kaya mas malawak ang puwang na malalampasan ng spark!
fact_en:
Can a spark jump across a big gap of air?

Yes! A larger electric charge creates higher voltage, letting the spark jump across a wider gap!

title: Spark hindi Apoy
fact_tl:
Ang ba ang static spark ay parang maliit na apoy?

Hindi! Ang static spark ay hindi nananatiling apoy. Isa lang itong mabilis na kislap ng kuryente sa hangin. Pwede itong magsindi ng apoy, pero ang spark mismo ay hindi apoy!
fact_en:
Is a static spark a tiny fire?

Nope! A static spark doesn't stay burning. It's just a fast flash of electricity in the air. It can start a fire, but the spark itself is not fire!

title: Walang Tulak Pablabas
fact_tl: Hindi ka itinutulak palabas kapag umiikot! Gusto ng katawan mong magpatuloy nang tuwid, pero ang pag-ikot ay humihila sa iyo papasok—kaya pakiramdam mong itinutulak ka palabas.
fact_en: Spinning doesn't push you outward! Your body wants to go straight, but the turning pulls you inward—making it feel like you're pushed out.

title: Radyo Balita Milyong Tahanan
fact_tl:
Paano binago ng radyo ang pagbabalita?

Binago ng radyo ang balita! Sabay-sabay nang dumating ang balita, babala sa bagyo, at musika sa milyon-milyong tahanan, kahit walang internet o TV.
fact_en:
How did the radio change the news?

Radio changed the news! News, storm warnings, and music reached millions of homes at the same time, even without internet or TV.

title: Steam Engine ni James Watt
fact_tl:
Ano ang pinapatakbo ng steam engine?

Pinaunlad ni James Watt noong 1700s, ang steam engine ay gumagamit ng singaw ng kumukulong tubig para sa makina, nagdulot ng pabrika, tren, at barko!
fact_en:
What did the steam engine power?

Improved by James Watt in the 1700s, the steam engine uses boiling water steam to power machines, leading to factories, trains, and ships!

title: Unang Motor Car ni Karl Benz
fact_tl: Ginawa ni Karl Benz ang unang motor car noong 1886! Nang gawing mura ni Henry Ford ang mga ito, nakapagbiyahe na ang tao nang walang kabayo o karwahe.
fact_en: Karl Benz built the first motor car in 1886! Later, Henry Ford made them cheap, so ordinary people could travel without horses or carriages.

title: Telegrapho Morse Code Kawad
fact_tl:
Paano nagpadala ng mabilis na mensahe ang telegrapo?

Pinaunlad ni Samuel Morse noong 1840s, ang telegrapo ay nagpadala ng mabilis na mensahe sa malayo gamit ang mga tuldok at guhit (Morse code) sa kawad!
fact_en:
How did the telegraph send fast messages?

Developed by Samuel Morse in the 1840s, the telegraph sent fast long-distance messages using dots and dashes (Morse code) through a wire!

title: Refrigerator Malamig Pagkain
fact_tl: Binago ng refrigerator ang buhay sa pagpapanatili ng pagkain sa malamig para hindi madaling mapanis! Maitatago na ang pagkain nang matagal nang hindi kailangan ng yelo araw-araw.
fact_en: The refrigerator changed life by keeping food cold so it doesn't spoil quickly! People could store food for a long time without needing daily ice.

title: Kamera Liwanag Lente Larawan
fact_tl: Humuhuli ng larawan ang kamera sa pagpapasok ng liwanag sa lente! Naimbento noong 1800s, natala nito ang mga totoong larawan nang hindi iginuhit ng kamay.
fact_en: The camera captures images by letting light through a lens! Invented in the 1800s, it recorded real pictures for the first time without drawing by hand.

title: Mabilis Ikot vs Tuwid Takbo
fact_tl: Ang mabilis na pag-ikot ay iba sa mabilis na pagtakbo nang tuwid! Ang umiikot ay nasa iisang lugar lang, pero ang tumatakbo ay lumilipat. Pareho silang mabilis na galaw!
fact_en: Spinning fast is different from moving fast in a straight line! A spinning object stays in one spot, while a moving object travels to a new place. Both are fast motion!

title: Balancing Pabigat Gulong Kotse
fact_tl:
Bakit may maliliit na pabigat ang gulong ng sasakyan?

Kapag mabilis ang pag-ikot ng gulong, kahit maliit na hindi pantay na timbang ay nagiging malakas na pagyanig! Nilalagyan ito ng pabigat para hindi mauga ang sasakyan.
fact_en:
Why do car tires have tiny weights?

When a tire spins fast, a tiny uneven weight causes a strong shake! Little weights are added so it spins evenly, keeping the car from vibrating at high speed.

title: Salad Spinner Tuyo Gulay
fact_tl: Ang salad spinner ay isang basket na pinapaikot nang mabilis para patuyuin ang hinugasang gulay! Tumitilapon ang tubig sa mga butas, kaya natutuyo ang dahon nang hindi mo kailangang pisilin.
fact_en: A salad spinner is a basket you spin fast to dry washed vegetables! As it turns, water is flung out through the holes, drying the leaves without squeezing them.

title: CD Disc Ikot Laser Data
fact_tl: Sa CD o DVD player, kailangang umiikot ang disc para mabasa ng laser ang impormasyon! Kapag mas mabilis ang pag-ikot, mas mabilis ding nababasa ng laser ang mga bahagi.
fact_en: In a CD or DVD player, the disc must spin so a laser can read its stored information! The faster the disc spins, the faster the laser reads the data.

title: Blender Talim Durugin Prutas
fact_tl: Ang blender ay may talim na umiikot nang napakabilis para durugin ang prutas o yelo! Tinatama nito ang pagkain nang libu-libong beses sa ilang segundo, kaya nagiging makinis na shake.
fact_en: A blender has a blade that spins very fast to crush fruit or ice! It hits the food thousands of times in seconds, turning it into a smooth shake.

title: Drill Ikot Butas Kahoy
fact_tl: Ang drill ay may matulis na bahagi na umiikot nang napakabilis para gumawa ng butas sa kahoy o pader! Mas mabilis ang pag-ikot, mas madali itong humukay, kaya mas mabilis matapos.
fact_en: A drill has a sharp bit that spins very fast to make holes in wood or walls! The faster it spins, the easier it digs in, making the hole quickly.

title: Wobble Hindi Pantay Timbang Fan
fact_tl:
Umuuga ba ang ceiling fan dahil lang mabilis itong umikot?

Hindi! Umuuga ito kapag hindi pantay ang timbang ng mga talim, tulad ng mas maraming alikabok sa isa. Pinapalala lang ng bilis ito.
fact_en:
Does a ceiling fan wobble just because it spins fast?

Nope! It wobbles when blades aren't evenly weighted, like having more dust on one. Speed just makes it worse, but isn't the real cause.

title: Centrifuge Dugo Hiwalay Bahagi
fact_tl:
Paano mabilis na ihihiwalay ng mga ospital ang mga bahagi ng dugo?

May makinang tinatawag na centrifuge na umiikot nang sobrang bilis! Ang mas mabibigat na bahagi ay napupunta sa ilalim, at ang magagaan sa itaas.
fact_en:
How do hospitals separate the parts of blood so quickly?

A machine called a centrifuge spins blood very fast! The heavier parts settle at the bottom, while the lighter parts stay on top.

title: Stainless Spoon Magnet Hindi
fact_tl: Hindi lahat ng steel ay dumidikit sa magnet! Ang ibang stainless steel spoons ay hindi, dahil may halo itong ibang metal na nagpapabago sa domains.
fact_en: Not all steel sticks to magnets! Some stainless steel spoons don't stick because it's mixed with other metals that change how the domains line up.

title: Plastic Kahoy Hindi Magnetic
fact_tl: Hindi humihila ang magnet sa plastic, wood, paper, cloth, o rubber! Hindi sila metal, kaya walang domains na mag-a-align, at hindi sila didikit.
fact_en: Magnets don't pull plastic, wood, paper, cloth, or rubber! Since they aren't metals, they have no domains to line up, so they won't stick.

title: Tunay na Ginto Hindi Magnet
fact_tl:
Kayang sabihin ng magnet kung tunay ba ang iyong 'gintong' alahas?

Ang tunay na ginto ay hindi tumutugon sa magnet! Kapag dumikit ang alahas, malamang may halo itong ibang metal—hindi purong ginto. Pero tandaan: may mga peke na hindi rin magnetic!
fact_en:
Can a magnet tell if your 'gold' jewelry is real?

Real gold ignores magnets completely! If jewelry sticks, it likely has other metals mixed in—not pure gold. But watch out: some fakes aren't magnetic either!

title: Aluminum Laruan Hindi Dikit
fact_tl:
Bakit hindi dumudumikit ang pinakamalakas mong magnet sa isang laruan?

Kahit pinakamalakas na magnet, hindi kayang hilahin ang mga laruan na aluminum o plastik! Hindi ito tungkol sa lakas ng magnet—kung walang iron ang laruan, talagang hindi ito didikit.
fact_en:
Why won't your strongest magnet stick to a toy?

Even the strongest magnet can't pull aluminum or plastic toys! It's not about magnet strength—if the toy has no iron inside, it simply won't stick, no matter what.

title: Gunting Blade Dikit Handle Hindi
fact_tl: May mga bagay na may magnetic at non-magnetic parts! Dumidikit ang magnet sa steel blades ng gunting, pero hindi sa plastic handles. Depende ito sa bahaging tinitest mo!
fact_en: Some objects have both magnetic and non-magnetic parts! A magnet sticks to the steel blades of scissors, but not the plastic handles. It depends on the part you test!

title: Mata Liwanag Tainga Tunog
fact_tl:
Paano natin nakikita at naririnig ang mundo sa paligid?

Nakikita natin gamit ang ilaw, at naririnig natin gamit ang tunog! Ang ilaw ay umaabot sa mata, samantalang ang tunog ay umaabot sa tainga. Magkaiba silang dalawang paraan!
fact_en:
How do we see and hear the world around us?

We see using light, and we hear using sound! Light reaches the eyes, while sound reaches the ears. These are two different ways we sense the world.

title: Opaque Bato Kahoy Block Anino
fact_tl: May mga bagay na opaque tulad ng bato, kahoy, o katawan natin, kaya hindi dumadaan ang ilaw! Dahil hinaharang nila ang ilaw, nabubuo ang anino sa likod nila.
fact_en: Some things are opaque, like stone, wood, or our bodies, so light does not pass through! Because they block the light, a shadow forms behind them.

title: Dim Liwanag Hirap Makakita
fact_tl: Kapag madilim, mas mahirap makakita dahil kaunti lang ang ilaw na tumatalbog sa mga bagay papunta sa ating mata! Kapag dumami ang ilaw, mas malinaw nating nakikita ang paligid.
fact_en: When it is dim, it is harder to see because only a little light bounces off objects toward our eyes! When there is more light, we see our surroundings more clearly.

title: Bituin Liwanag Nakaraan Oras
fact_tl:
Bakit ang mga bituin ay nagpapakita ng nakaraan?

Napakabilis ng ilaw, pero mula sa malalayong bituin, matagal itong dumating! Kapag tumingin ka sa bituin, nakikita mo ang ilaw mula noong nakaraan.
fact_en:
Why do stars show us the past?

Light travels super fast, but from distant stars, it takes a long time! When you look at a star, you see light from long ago.

title: Bakal na Puso
fact_tl:
Paano mo papalakasin ang isang electromagnet?

Maglagay ng bakal na pako sa gitna ng coil! Pinapalakas ng bakal ang magnetic force mula sa kuryente, kaya mas marami itong nahihilang bagay.
fact_en:
How can you make an electromagnet stronger?

Put an iron nail in the middle of the coil! The iron boosts the magnetic force from the electricity, making it strong enough to pull more objects.

title: Permanent Fridge Magnet Laging
fact_tl: Ang permanent magnet, tulad ng sa ref, ay laging magnetic kahit walang kuryente. Pero ang electromagnet ay nagiging magnet lang kapag may dumadaloy na kuryente. Iyan ang pagkakaiba nila!
fact_en: A permanent magnet, like your fridge magnet, is always magnetic without electricity. But an electromagnet only works while electricity flows through it. That’s their main difference!

title: Electromagnet Wire Loop Battery
fact_tl: Gusto mo ng mas malakas na electromagnet? Dagdagan mo ang mga ikot ng kawad sa coil, o gumamit ng mas malakas na baterya! Mas maraming ikot at kuryente, mas malakas ang magnet.
fact_en: Want a stronger electromagnet? Add more wire loops to the coil, or use a more powerful battery! More loops and more current equal a stronger magnet.

title: Electromagnet Battery Ubos
fact_tl: Biglang hindi na kumakapit ang gawa mong electromagnet? Malamang ubos na ang baterya! Walang kuryente, walang magnet. Palitan mo lang ang baterya, at babalik ang lakas nito!
fact_en: Did your homemade electromagnet suddenly stop sticking? The battery probably ran out! No electricity means no magnet. Just replace the battery, and its strength comes back!

title: Electromagnet Relay Makina
fact_tl: Sa loob ng maraming makina, ang electromagnet ay nagsisilbing switch. Gamit ang maliit na current, ligtas nitong sinusindihan o pinapatay ang malalaking makina!
fact_en: Inside many machines, an electromagnet acts as a switch. Using just a small current, it safely turns large, dangerous machines on or off!

title: Electromagnet Mainit Wire
fact_tl: Kapag matagal ang electromagnet, umiinit ang wire at battery. Normal lang ito dahil nagiging init ang ilang kuryente!
fact_en: If you run an electromagnet too long, the wire and battery get warm. This is normal since some electricity turns into heat!

title: Hertz Frequency Wave Segundo
fact_tl: Ang frequency ay sinusukat sa hertz (Hz). Ang isang hertz ay isang kumpletong wave kada segundo, kaya 10 Hz ay sampung wave bawat segundo!
fact_en: Frequency is measured in hertz (Hz). One hertz means one complete wave passes by each second, so 10 Hz means ten waves per second!

title: Period Wave Kabaligtaran
fact_tl: Ang period ay ang oras para sa isang buong wave! Ito ang kabaliktaran ng frequency. Mataas na frequency ay maikling period. Sa 4 Hz, ang period ay 0.25 seconds lang!
fact_en: The period is the time for one whole wave! It's the opposite of frequency. High frequency means a short period. At 4 Hz, the period is just 0.25 seconds!

title: Vibration Bilis Frequency Source
fact_tl:
Ano ang nagpapataas o nagpapababa ng frequency ng isang wave?

Nakadepende ito sa bilis ng vibration ng source! Mabilis na kumukurap na kuwerdas ng gitara ay may mataas na frequency, at mabagal ay mababa.
fact_en:
What makes a wave's frequency high or low?

It depends on how fast the source vibrates! A fast vibrating guitar string has high frequency, while a slow one has low frequency.

title: Frequency kumpara Amplitude Wave
fact_tl: Huwag malito ang frequency at amplitude! Ang frequency ay kung ilang waves ang dumadaan per second, ang amplitude naman ay kung gaano kataas. Sa tunog, frequency ang pitch, amplitude ang loudness!
fact_en: Don't confuse frequency and amplitude! Frequency is how many waves pass per second, while amplitude is how tall the wave is. In sound, frequency decides pitch, and amplitude decides loudness!

title: Tao Dinig 20 Hz 20000 Range
fact_tl:
Anong mga tunog ang kayang marinig ng ating tainga?

Nakakarinig lang tayo ng frequencies mula 20 Hz hanggang 20,000 Hz! Hindi natin naririnig ang nasa labas nito, pero ang mga hayop tulad ng aso ay nakakarinig ng mas mataas!
fact_en:
What sounds can our human ears actually hear?

We only hear frequencies from 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz! We can't hear sounds outside this, but animals like dogs can hear much higher frequencies than us!

title: Bilangin ang Waves kada Segundo
fact_tl: Gustong malaman ang frequency? Bilangin mo lang kung ilang complete waves ang dumadaan sa isang punto in one second! Kung lima sa bato sa dagat, 5 Hz na iyon!
fact_en: Want to find the frequency? Just count how many complete waves pass a point in one second! If five waves pass a sea rock in one second, it's 5 Hz!

title: Ultrasound Ospital Baby Tiyan
fact_tl: Sa mga ospital sa Pilipinas, gumagamit ang ultrasound ng super high frequency na hindi marinig ng tao! Tumatalbog ito sa loob para makagawa ng larawan, tulad ng baby sa tiyan ni mom.
fact_en: In Philippine hospitals, ultrasound uses a super high frequency humans can't hear! This sound bounces inside to make a picture, like seeing a baby in mom's belly.

title: Ambulansya Siren Palapit Palayo
fact_tl: Kapag papalapit ang ambulansya, naipit ang sound waves kaya tumataas ang frequency at mas matinis ang tunog. Kapag papalayo na, kumakalat ang waves kaya bumababa ang frequency!
fact_en: When an ambulance approaches, sound waves squeeze together, making the frequency rise and the sound higher. As it moves away, waves spread out and the frequency drops!

title: Natural Frequency Duyan Bell
fact_tl: Bawat bagay ay may natural frequency kung saan pinakamadali itong yumanig! Tulak mo ang duyan sa tamang ritmo at lalo itong tumataas. Kaya may natatanging tunog ang bawat bell at instrument.
fact_en: Every object has a natural frequency where it vibrates easily! Push a swing at the right rhythm and it goes higher. This is why every bell has its own distinct sound.

title: Cellphone Radio Globe Smart
fact_tl: Gumagamit ang cellphone mo ng radio waves na may specific frequencies para sa calls at texts! Iba't ibang frequencies ang ginagamit ng Globe at Smart sa Pilipinas para hindi magsalubong ang signals.
fact_en: Your cellphone uses radio waves of specific frequencies for calls and texts! Globe and Smart in the Philippines use different frequencies so their signals do not interfere with each other.

title: EM Spectrum Ayos Frequency
fact_tl: Ang electromagnetic spectrum ay isang malaking pamilya ng waves na nakaayos ayon sa frequency! Mula sa low-frequency radio waves hanggang high-frequency gamma rays, pareho silang uri ng wave, frequency lang ang pagkakaiba.
fact_en: The electromagnetic spectrum is a big family of waves arranged by frequency! From low-frequency radio waves up to high-frequency gamma rays, they are all the same kind of wave, differing only in frequency.

title: Puwersa ng Kalabaw
fact_tl:
Paano nakakapagalaw ng kariton ang kalabaw?

Gumagamit ang kalabaw ng puwersa! Ang malakas niyang hila ay nagpapagalaw sa kariton pasulong.
fact_en:
How does a carabao move a heavy cart?

The carabao uses force! Its strong pull makes the cart move forward on the road.

title: Momentum kg m/s Yunit
fact_tl:
Paano natin sinusukat ang momentum, at saan galing ang kakaibang yunit nito?

Sinusukat ang momentum sa kilogram-metro kada segundo (kg·m/s)! Pinagsama nito ang yunit ng masa (kilogram) at bilis (metro kada segundo) kapag pinarami sila.
fact_en:
How do we measure momentum, and where does its cool unit come from?

Momentum is measured in kilogram-meters per second (kg·m/s)! It combines the units for mass (kilograms) and velocity (meters per second) when you multiply them together.

title: Mabilis Maliit = Mabagal Mabigat
fact_tl:
Pwede bang magkaparehong momentum ang isang maliit na napakabilis at isang malaking mabagal?

Oo! Ang magaan pero napakabilis ay pwedeng magkapareho ng momentum sa mabigat pero mabagal. Ang maliit na bala ay may malaking momentum dahil sobrang bilis nito!
fact_en:
Can a tiny, super-fast object have the same momentum as a huge, slow one?

Yes! A light but very fast object can match a heavy, slow one. A small bullet has huge momentum because it travels extremely fast, even though it's light!

title: Nakatigil Zero Momentum
fact_tl:
Ano ang nangyayari sa momentum ng isang napakabigat na bagay kapag ito ay nakatigil?

Ang momentum nito ay zero! Kahit gaano pa kabigat, kung walang bilis o galaw, walang momentum.
fact_en:
What happens to the momentum of a super heavy object when it is completely still?

Its momentum is exactly zero! No matter how heavy it is, without velocity or movement, there is simply no momentum at all.

title: Doble Masa Doble Momentum
fact_tl: Kung idoble mo ang masa ng isang bagay sa parehong bilis, dodoblehin din ang momentum nito! Laging tumataas ang momentum nang sabay sa masa.
fact_en: If you double an object's mass but keep the same speed, its momentum doubles too! Momentum always increases in perfect step with the mass.

title: Hindi Bilis Lang Masa rin
fact_tl:
Ang bilis lang ba ang mahalaga sa momentum?

Hindi! Kasing-halaga rin ang masa. Ang mabagal pero napakabigat na bagay ay pwedeng magkaroon ng malaking momentum!
fact_en:
Does only speed matter for momentum?

Nope! Mass is just as important. A slow but very heavy object can still have a large momentum!

title: Basketball Masakit Saluhin
fact_tl:
Bakit mas masakit saluhin ang mabigat na basketball kaysa magaan na tennis ball sa parehong bilis?

Mas malaki ang momentum ng mabigat na bola! Mas maraming galaw ang kailangang pigilan ng kamay mo.
fact_en:
Why does catching a heavy basketball hurt more than a light tennis ball at the same speed?

The heavy ball has more momentum! Your hands must stop more motion.

title: Momentum ng Kariton
fact_tl:
Bakit mahirap itulak at patigilin ang punong-puno na kariton sa palengke?

Dahil malaki ang momentum nito! Mas mabigat ang kariton, mas malaki ang momentum nito kapag gumagalaw.
fact_en:
Why is a fully loaded market cart so hard to push and stop?

Because it has large momentum! The heavier the cart, the more momentum it has when moving.

title: Radio Wave Mahabang Wavelength
fact_tl:
Bakit kaya ng radio waves na maglakbay nang malayo at umikot sa mga building?

Ang radio waves ang may pinakamahabang wavelength sa electromagnetic spectrum—ang iba ay mas mahaba pa sa bahay! Kaya sila nakakalikot sa mga hadlang at nakakalakbay nang napakalayo.
fact_en:
Why can radio waves travel so far and bend around buildings?

Radio waves have the longest wavelength in the electromagnetic spectrum—some are even longer than a house! This lets them bend around obstacles and travel very far.

title: Isang Frequency, Isang Station
fact_tl:
Paano nakakapili ang radyo mo ng isang station nang hindi nagkahalo lahat?

Bawat radio station ay nagsasahimpapawid sa sarili nitong frequency, kaya hindi sila nag-o-overlap. Kapag tine-tune mo ang radyo, pinipili mo kung anong frequency ang sasaluhin—kaya malinaw ang isang station!
fact_en:
How does your radio pick just one station without mixing them all up?

Each radio station broadcasts on its own unique frequency, so they don't overlap. When you tune your radio, you're picking which frequency to catch—that's why you hear one station clearly!

title: Natural Radio Waves
fact_tl:
Tao lang ba ang gumagawa ng radio waves?

Hindi! Ang mga bituin, galaksiya, at Araw ay natural na naglalabas ng radio waves. Ginagamit ng mga astronomo ang malalaking radio telescope para pakinggan at aralin ang kalawakan!
fact_en:
Do only humans make radio waves?

Nope! Stars, galaxies, and the Sun naturally give off radio waves. Astronomers use giant radio telescopes to listen to them and explore distant space!

title: GPS Signal mula Satellite
fact_tl: Ang GPS ng cellphone mo ay nakakakuha ng radio signals mula sa mga satellite! Sa pagsukat kung gaano katagal dumating ang bawat signal, naku-kwenta nito kung nasaan ka sa mapa.
fact_en: Your phone's GPS catches radio signals from satellites in the sky! By measuring how long each signal takes to arrive, it calculates exactly where you are on the map.

title: Layong Humihinang Signal
fact_tl: Habang lumalayo ang radio waves, kumakalat ang energy nila kaya humihina ang signal! Kaya nagiging maingay o nawawala ang radyo kapag malayo ka na sa transmission tower.
fact_en: As radio waves travel farther, their energy spreads out, making the signal weaker! That is why your radio station gets noisy or fades out when you drive far from the tower.

title: Heinrich Hertz 1880s
fact_tl:
Sino ang nakatuklas ng radio waves?

Noong huling bahagi ng 1880s, si Heinrich Hertz ang unang nakagawa at nakapagpatunay ng radio waves sa kanyang lab! Ang yunit ng frequency na 'hertz' ay ipinangalan bilang parangal sa kanya.
fact_en:
Who discovered radio waves?

In the late 1880s, Heinrich Hertz was the first to produce and prove radio waves in his lab! The frequency unit 'hertz' is named to honor him.

title: Static laban Sliding
fact_tl: Mas mahirap simulan ang paggalaw ng nakatigil na bagay kaysa padayunin! Ang unang tulak sa mabigat na aparador ang pinakamahirap — kapag gumalaw na, mas madali. Mas malakas ang friction sa nakatigil!
fact_en: It's harder to start a still object moving than to keep it going! The first push on a heavy cabinet is toughest — once sliding, it's easier. Friction is stronger on still objects!

title: Langis Makina Friction Bawas
fact_tl: Para babaan ang friction, nilalagyan ng langis ang mga bahagi ng makina! Ang langis ay nagpapadulas para hindi direktang magkiskis. Nilalagyan ng langis ang kadena ng bisikleta — para magaan at hindi kalawangin!
fact_en: To lower friction, we put oil on machine parts! The oil creates a thin slippery layer so surfaces don't rub directly. We oil bike chains to run smoothly and prevent rust!

title: Gulong Treads Grip Basag Daan
fact_tl: May mga ukit o treads ang gulong para dumami ang friction at kumapit sa kalsada, lalo na kapag basa! Kapag kapos na ang ukit, madulas na at delikado ito.
fact_en: Car tires have grooves called treads to increase friction and grip the road, especially when wet! If treads wear down, the tire gets slippery and dangerous.

title: Posporo Kahon Rough Apoy
fact_tl: Ang pagkiskis ng posporo sa magaspang na kahon ay gumagawa ng friction at init para pumutok! Kailangan mo ng magaspang na ibabaw para sa sapat na friction; hindi gagana sa makinis!
fact_en: Striking a match on the rough box creates friction, which makes heat to light the chemical! You need that rough surface for enough friction; a smooth one won't work!

title: Friction Tulong Lakad Brake
fact_tl: Hindi palaging masama ang friction! Kung wala ito, hindi tayo makakalakad, hindi makakapreno ang sasakyan, at hindi mahahawakan ang lapis. Kailangan natin ito sa maraming bagay!
fact_en: Friction isn't always bad! Without it, we couldn't walk, cars couldn't brake, and we couldn't hold a pencil. We actually need friction for many everyday things!

title: Puno Box Mabigat Friction
fact_tl:
Bakit mas mahirap itulak ang punong kahon kaysa sa walang laman?

Dahil mas malaki ang friction kapag mas mabigat! Ang bigat ay mas idinidiin ang mga ibabaw kaya mas malakas magkiskis. Mas mabigat, mas malaking friction!
fact_en:
Why is a full box harder to push than an empty one?

Because heavier objects have greater friction! The weight presses the surfaces together harder, making them rub more. So, heavier always means more friction!

title: Bike Brake Goma Pad Wheel
fact_tl:
Paano gumagamit ang preno ng bisikleta ng friction para tumigil?

May goma na dumidiin sa gulong! Ang friction sa pagitan nila ang nagpapabagal at nagpapatigil. Kapag basa ang preno, mas mahina ang friction at mas matagal tumigil!
fact_en:
How do bike brakes use friction to stop?

A rubber pad presses the wheel! The friction between them slows and stops the bike. If brakes are wet, friction is weaker and it takes longer to stop!

title: Pambura at Friction
fact_tl:
Paano ba gumagana ang pambura?

Gumagamit ng friction ang pagbubura! Kinukuskos ng pambura ang maliliit na graphite marks. Kailangan mong idiin at ikiskis, o walang mababura!
fact_en:
How does an eraser actually work?

Erasing uses friction! Rubbing the eraser scrubs off tiny graphite marks. You must press and rub, or nothing gets erased!

title: Time Axis Laging Pasulong Graph
fact_tl:
Bakit hindi pwedeng pumunta sa kaliwa ang linya sa graph?

Sa distance-time graph, ang oras sa horizontal axis ay palaging gumagalaw pasulong! Hindi ito bumabalik, kaya hindi pwedeng pumunta sa kaliwa ang linya—laging sa kanan.
fact_en:
Why can't a graph line go left?

On a distance-time graph, time on the horizontal axis always moves forward! It never goes back, so lines can never go left—time always flows right.

title: Matarik, Mabilis
fact_tl:
Paano malalaman kung alin ang mas mabilis sa graph?

Sa distance-time graph, ang mas matarik na linya ay sa mas mabilis na sasakyan! Kung mas matarik ang linya ng jeepney kaysa tricycle, mas mabilis ang jeepney!
fact_en:
How to spot the faster vehicle on a graph?

On a distance-time graph, the steeper line belongs to the faster vehicle! If a jeepney's line is steeper than a tricycle's, the jeepney is faster—no numbers needed!

title: Graph Linya Tawid Magkatabi
fact_tl: Kapag nagsalubong ang dalawang linya sa distance-time graph, parehong layo na ang dalawang bagay sa parehong oras! Magkasama sila sa iisang lugar, o naabutan ng isa ang isa.
fact_en: When two lines cross on a distance-time graph, both objects are at the exact same distance and time! They are together at the same spot, or one caught up.

title: Graph Steep Bilis Hindi Taas
fact_tl: Akala mo pinakamataas ay pinakamabilis sa distance-time graph? Hindi! Ang bilis ay nasa TARIK ng linya, hindi sa taas. Mataas pero patag na linya? Ibig sabihin, nakatigil ka na!
fact_en: Think highest means fastest on a distance-time graph? Nope! Speed comes from the STEEPNESS of the line, not height. A high but flat line means you actually stopped!

title: Walang Vertical Line
fact_tl:
Puwedeng magkaroon ng perpektong patindig na linya sa distance-time graph?

Hindi! Ibig sabihin niyon ay lumayo nang walang oras na lumipas. Walang-hangganang bilis iyon, na imposible sa totoong buhay!
fact_en:
Can a perfectly vertical line exist on a distance-time graph?

No! That would mean jumping a distance in zero time. That means infinite speed, which is totally impossible in real life!

title: Tangent Linya Bilis Sandali
fact_tl:
Paano malalaman ang eksaktong bilis sa isang sandali sa kurbadong linya?

Gumuhit ng tuwid na linya (tangent) na dumidikit lang sa kurba sa puntong iyon! Ang slope ng tangent na iyon ang bilis sa sandaling iyon.
fact_en:
How do you find the exact speed at one instant on a curved line?

Draw a straight line, called a tangent, that just touches the curve at that exact point! The slope of that tangent is the speed at that moment.

title: Parallel na Line Parehong Bilis
fact_tl:
Ano ang ibig sabihin ng parallel na linya sa distance-time graph?

Ang parallel na linya ay parehong bilis! Baka nauna lang ang isa, pero pareho silang bumibiyahe sa iisang bilis — hindi lang sila magsasalubong.
fact_en:
What do parallel lines on a distance-time graph tell us?

Parallel lines mean both objects move at the same speed! One might have left earlier, but they travel at one equal speed — they just never meet.

title: Mass hindi Laki o Hugis
fact_tl: Ang inertia ay nakadepende lang sa masa — hindi sa laki o hugis! Mas mahirap igalaw ang maliit na bolang bakal kaysa malaking beach ball dahil mas maraming masa ang bakal.
fact_en: Inertia depends only on mass — not size or shape! A small iron ball is harder to move than a big beach ball because iron has more mass, even if smaller.

title: Inertia, Hindi Force
fact_tl: Hindi puwersa ang inertia na nagtutulak o humahatak! Ito ay isang katangian lang na nagsasabing gaano kahirap baguhin ang kilos ng bagay.
fact_en: Inertia is not a force that pushes or pulls! It’s just a property describing how hard it is to change an object's motion.

title: Crepuscular na Sinag
fact_tl:
Ano ang tawag sa mga sinag ng araw na dumadaan sa pagitan ng mga ulap?

Ang tawag dito ay crepuscular rays! Ang alikabok at moisture sa hangin ang nagpapakita sa mga beam-like na sinag ng araw.
fact_en:
What are those sunbeams shining through cloud gaps?

They are crepuscular rays! Dust and moisture in the air make these beam-like shafts of sunlight visible.

title: Inertia Direksyon Kotse LikoS
fact_tl: Nilalabanan ng inertia ang pagbabago ng direksyon, hindi lang paghinto! Kapag mabilis na lumiko ang sasakyan, parang naitutulak ka palabas dahil gusto pa ng katawan mong dumiretso.
fact_en: Inertia resists changing direction, not just starting or stopping! When a car turns sharply, your body wants to keep going straight, so you feel pushed outward.

title: Malapit sa Turnilyo
fact_tl:
Saan mo igupit ang makapal na bagay?

Ilagay malapit sa turnilyo, hindi sa dulo! Mas malakas ang gupit doon dahil mas malapit sa fulcrum.
fact_en:
Where should you cut something thick?

Put it near the screw, not at the tip! The cut is stronger there because it is closer to the fulcrum.

title: Kidlat Muna Kulog Oras Biyahe
fact_tl:
Bakit umaabot muna ang kidlat bago ang kulog?

May oras ang pagbiyahe ng tunog at mas mabagal ito kaysa liwanag! Sa bagyo, agad nakikita ang kidlat, pero mas matagal dumating ang kulog sa tainga.
fact_en:
Why do you see lightning before hearing thunder?

Sound takes time to travel and is much slower than light! During a storm, light reaches your eyes instantly, but the thunder takes longer to reach your ears.

title: Tunog Walang Hangin Kalawakan
fact_tl: Kailangan ng tunog ng hangin, tubig, o solido para dumaloy! Sa outer space, walang hangin kaya tahimik ito. Kahit sumabog ang bituin, walang maririnig dahil walang dadaanan ang tunog.
fact_en: Sound needs air, water, or solids to travel! In outer space, there's no air, so it's silent. Even an exploding star makes no sound because there's nothing to carry it.

title: Walang Lamang Kuwarto Echo
fact_tl: Sa bakanteng kwarto, tumatalbog ang tunog sa hubad na pader kaya malakas at may echo! Pero kapag may sofa, carpet, o kurtina, hinihigop nila ang tunog kaya mas malambot at walang echo.
fact_en: In an empty room, sound bounces off bare walls, making it loud and echoey! But a sofa, carpet, or curtains soak up the sound, making it softer with no echo.

title: Maingay na Kalye Jeepney Tindera
fact_tl:
Bakit napakaingay ng mga abalang kalye sa Pilipinas?

Busina ng jeepney, sigaw ng tindera, at tugtog ng sari-sari store ay sabay-sabay sa hangin! Dahil kumakalat ang tunog sa lahat ng direksyon at sumasalubong, napakaingay ng paligid.
fact_en:
Why are busy Philippine streets so noisy?

Jeepney horns, shouting vendors, and store music all travel through the air at once! Since sound spreads in every direction and these sounds meet, the whole place becomes very noisy.

title: Tahimik na Hangin Tunog Daloy
fact_tl: Hindi kailangan ng umiihip na hangin para makarinig! Kahit tahimik, nakakarating pa rin ang tunog. Hindi lumilipad ang hangin papunta sa iyo; nagtutulak-tulakan lang ang maliliit na particles para ipasa ito.
fact_en: You don't need blowing wind to hear sound! Even in calm air, sound travels. The air doesn't fly to you; its tiny particles just gently push one another to pass the sound.

title: Malambot Unan Kurtina Higop
fact_tl: Ang malalambot na bagay tulad ng unan at kurtina ay humihigop ng tunog! Kaya mahina ang sigaw sa unan, at gumagamit ng malalambot na pader ang recording studio para makulong ang tunog.
fact_en: Soft things like pillows and curtains soak up sound instead of bouncing it! Shouting into a pillow makes a muffled sound, which is why recording studios use soft walls to trap sound.

title: Ramdam sa Sahing Vibration Trak
fact_tl: Hindi lang sa tainga nararamdaman ang tunog—minsan, ramdam din sa katawan! Kapag dumaan ang mabigat na trak o tumalon ang maraming bata, naipapasa ang vibration sa sahig, kaya nararamdaman mong yumayanig ito.
fact_en: We don't just hear sound with our ears; sometimes we feel it! When a heavy truck passes or kids jump, the vibration travels through the ground, making the floor shake under your feet.

title: Grounding Daan Elektron Lupa
fact_tl: Kapag may sobrang static charge, ang grounding ay nagbibigay ng madaling daan para makadaloy ang mga elektron sa lupa. Umaagos sila hanggang maging balanced at neutral muli ang bagay!
fact_en: When an object has extra static charge, grounding gives electrons an easy path to flow to the ground. They keep flowing until the object is balanced and neutral again!

title: Lightning Rod Bubong Wire Lupa
fact_tl: Ang lightning rod sa bubong ay totoong gamit ng grounding! Ito ay metal na nakakonekta sa lupa sa makapal na wire. Kapag tumama ang kidlat, dadalhin nito ang malaking charge pababa.
fact_en: A lightning rod on a roof uses grounding! It's a metal point connected to the ground by a thick wire. When lightning strikes, it safely carries the huge charge down.

title: Doorknob Spark Munting Grounding
fact_tl:
Bakit nakukuryente ka kapag hinawakan ang metal na doorknob?

Kapag naipon mo ang static charge sa paglalakad sa karpet, biglang nagri-ground ang katawan mo sa metal! Tumatalon ang mga elektron sa maliit na spark, at iyon ang kuryap na naramdaman mo.
fact_en:
Why do you get a shock when touching a metal doorknob?

If you build up static charge walking on a carpet, your body suddenly grounds through the metal! Electrons jump in a tiny spark, and that quick jolt is what you feel.

title: Grounding Charge Hindi Wasak
fact_tl: Hindi nawawala ang charge kapag nag-ground! Hindi ito nasisira. Lumilipat lang ang mga elektron sa napakalaking Earth kung saan kumakalat sila at hindi na napapansin. Lumipat lang, hindi naglaho!
fact_en: Charge doesn't disappear when grounded! It is not destroyed. The electrons just move into the huge Earth where they spread out and become unnoticeable. They only moved; they did not vanish!

title: Grounding Path Insulator Block
fact_tl: Ang grounding ay nagbubukas ng daan para makadaloy ang charge sa lupa. Ang insulating naman ay humaharang para manatili ang charge sa isang lugar. Magkasalungat sila: ang isa ay nagpapalabas, ang isa ay nagpapanatili!
fact_en: Grounding opens a path so charge flows to the ground. Insulating blocks the flow so charge stays in one place. They are opposites: one lets charge escape, the other keeps it trapped.

title: Ikatlong Pin Ground Wire Plug
fact_tl: Napansin mo ba na may tatlong pin ang ilang saksak? Ang ikatlong pin ay ground wire! Kung may tumagas na kuryente sa metal ng appliance, dadalhin ito ng wire sa lupa para hindi ka makukuryente.
fact_en: Notice how some plugs have three pins? The third pin is the ground wire! If electricity leaks onto the metal body, this wire carries it safely to the ground to prevent shocks.

title: Fuel Truck Wire Lupa Bago Bomba
fact_tl: Bago magbomba ng gasolina, ikinakabit muna sa lupa ang trak gamit ang kawad! Tinatanggal nito ang static charge para walang spark na makapapag-apoy sa singaw.
fact_en: Before pumping fuel, trucks are connected to the ground with a wire! This removes static charge so no tiny spark starts a fire near the fuel vapor.

title: Sobrang Charge Lang Umalis
fact_tl:
Inuubos ba ng grounding ang LAHAT ng kuryente sa isang bagay?

Hindi! Ang sobrang charge lang ang aalis. Titigil ang daloy kapag naging balanced o neutral na ang bagay. Kapag pantay na ang positive at negative charges, wala nang itutulak palabas!
fact_en:
Does grounding drain ALL the electricity from an object?

Nope! Only the extra charge leaves. The flow stops once the object is balanced or neutral. When positive and negative charges are equal, nothing is left to push out!

title: Humid PH Static Leak Mabilis
fact_tl: Sa mahalumigmig na Pilipinas, mas mabilis mawala ang static charge! Ang manipis na tubig sa hangin ay nagsisilbing daan para dumaloy ang charge sa lupa, kaya iwas sa kuryap!
fact_en: In the humid Philippines, static charge leaks away faster! A thin layer of water in the air acts as a path to drain the charge to the ground, preventing shocks.

title: Isang Daliri Dahan Grounding
fact_tl: Gustong iwasan ang nakakakurot na spark? Bago hawakan ang doorknob, dahan-dahang hipuin muna ang metal o pader gamit ang isang daliri! Unti-unting aalis ang charge, kaya walang masakit na spark.
fact_en: Want to avoid a stinging spark? Before grabbing a doorknob, slowly touch the metal or wall with one finger! The charge drains gradually, so you won't feel a big spark.

title: Eroplano Static Wick Refuel
fact_tl:
Paano nagpapalabas ng static charge ang eroplano habang lumilipad?

Gumagamit ito ng maliliit na static wicks sa pakpak para ilabas ang charge sa hangin! Paglapag, ikinokonekta ito sa lupa bago mag-refuel para walang spark sa gasolina.
fact_en:
How do airplanes get rid of static charge while flying?

They use small static wicks on their wings to release the charge into the air! After landing, they connect to the ground before refueling to prevent sparks near the fuel.

title: Katawan Tao Daan Lupa Kuryente
fact_tl:
Puwede bang ang katawan mo mismo ang maging daan papunta sa lupa?

Oo! Ang tao ay nakakapagpadaloy ng kuryente. Kung walang goma sa sapatos, ang charge ay dadaloy mula sa kamay, sa katawan, sa paa, at papunta sa lupa!
fact_en:
Can your own body act as a path to the ground?

Yes! People conduct electricity a bit. If you stand without rubber shoes, charge can flow from your hand, through your body, down your feet, and right into the ground!

title: Grounding Daloy Dalawang Daan
fact_tl:
Palabas lang ba ang grounding?

Hindi! Kung ang object ay positive at kulang sa electrons, ang grounding ay nagpapadaloy ng electrons PAPASOK mula sa ground. Pwede itong palabas o papasok hanggang maging neutral!
fact_en:
Does grounding only push charge out?

Nope! If an object is positive and missing electrons, grounding lets electrons flow IN from the ground. Grounding goes both ways—out or in—until the object is neutral!

title: Tubo Metal Lupa Grounding Bahay
fact_tl: Sa maraming bahay, ang electrical system ay nakakonekta sa metal water pipe na nakabaon sa lupa. Magandang conductor ito papunta sa moist soil, kaya safe path ito para sa sobrang kuryente!
fact_en: In many homes, the electrical system connects to a metal water pipe buried in the ground. It's a great conductor to the moist soil, making a safe path for extra electricity!

title: Balloon Basang Kamay Laglag
fact_tl:
Bakit biglang nahuhulog ang dumidikit na balloon sa pader?

Kapag hinawakan mo ito ng basang kamay o metal, nag-ground ito! Dumaloy palabas ang charge, naging neutral ulit ang balloon, at biglang nawala ang dikit nito.
fact_en:
Why does a sticky balloon suddenly fall off the wall?

If you touch it with a wet hand or metal, it grounds! The charge flows out, the balloon becomes neutral again, and the sticking suddenly stops.

title: Kuskos Electron Jump Static
fact_tl:
Paano gumagawa ang pagkuskos ng static force?

Ang pagkuskos ay nagpapatalon ng maliliit na electrons mula sa isang object papunta sa isa! Ang mawawalan ay magiging positive, ang tatanggap ay negative. Attract sila sa isa't isa dahil magkasalungat ang charge nila!
fact_en:
How does rubbing things together create static force?

Rubbing makes tiny electrons jump from one object to another! The loser becomes positive, the winner becomes negative. These opposite charges attract each other!

title: Charge Neutral Papel Hila
fact_tl: Ang charged object ay kayang humila ng neutral paper! Kapag lumapit ito, naghihiwalay ang charges sa loob ng papel. Lumilipat ang opposite charge sa malapit na bahagi, kaya nahihila ang papel kahit neutral ito.
fact_en: A charged object can pull neutral paper! When close, charges inside the paper shift. The opposite charge moves to the near side, attracting the paper even with no overall charge.

title: Lobo at Static
fact_tl:
Paano makakapagdikit ang balloon sa pader nang walang pandikit?

Kuskusin mo lang ito sa buhok mo! Kukuha ang balloon ng static charge, na hihilahin ito sa pader para makadikit doon nang mag-isa!
fact_en:
How can a balloon stick to a wall without glue?

Just rub it on your hair! The balloon picks up a static charge, which pulls it to the wall so it clings there all by itself!

title: Tuyo Laba Damit Cling Elektron
fact_tl:
Bakit nagkakadikit ang damit pagkatuyo?

Habang naghahaluan at nagkukuskosan ang damit, naglilipat ang electron. Nagkakaroon sila ng magkapalitang charge at nag-a-attract, kaya nagdidikit sila!
fact_en:
Why do clothes cling together after drying?

As clothes tumble and rub, electrons move between them. They get opposite charges and attract each other, making them stick together like magic!

title: Static Cling Hindi Glue Stick
fact_tl: Walang pandikit sa lobo o damit! Puwersa ito mula sa static charge. Kayang-kaya mong tanggalin agad nang walang naiiwang malagkit na dumi.
fact_en: Balloons and clothes don't use glue to stick! It's an invisible force from static charge. You can pull them apart easily with no sticky mess left behind.

title: Plastik at Static
fact_tl:
Bakit madaling mag-static ang plastik pero hindi ang metal?

Sa plastik, naiipon ang charge dahil hindi ito gumagalaw! Sa metal, mabilis dumaloy ang charge kaya mahirap magka-static kapag hawak mo.
fact_en:
Why do plastics get static easily but metal doesn't?

On plastic, charge stays put and builds up! But on metal, charge flows away quickly, making it hard to build static while you're holding it.

title: Batas Newton Ikatlo
fact_tl: Kapag itinutulak mo ang tubig paatras gamit ang sagwan, tinutulak ka ng tubig paharap! Ito ang ikatlong batas ni Newton: bawat aksyon ay may katumbas na reaksyon.
fact_en: When you push water backward with a paddle, the water pushes you forward! This is Newton's third law: every action has an equal and opposite reaction.

title: Maria Cristina Talon
fact_tl:
Paano gumagawa ng kuryente ang Maria Cristina Falls?

Ang talon na ito sa Ilog Agus sa Iligan City ay gumagamit ng lakas ng bumabagsak na tubig para paikutin ang mga turbina at gumawa ng kuryente!
fact_en:
How does Maria Cristina Falls make electricity?

This waterfall on the Agus River in Iligan City uses the force of falling water to spin turbines and generate power!

title: Propeller at Sagwan
fact_tl:
Paano gumagana ang makina ng bangka tulad ng sagwan?

Ang propeller ay gumagana tulad ng sagwan! Ang umiikot na blades nito ay tumutulak ng tubig paatras, at ang tubig ay tumutulak sa bangka pasulong. Umiikot lang ito nang napakabilis at walang tigil — mas malakas kaysa kamay!
fact_en:
How is a boat engine like a paddle?

A propeller works just like a paddle! Its spinning blades push water backward, and the water pushes the boat forward. The propeller just spins super fast and never stops — way stronger than a hand!

title: Ibon Guwang Buto Hangin Mabaga
fact_tl:
Bakit magagaan ang mga ibon?

Maraming buto ng ibon ang hungkag o may butas sa loob (hollow bones)! Kaya magaan ang katawan nila, mas kaunting lakas na lang ang kailangan ng pakpak para itaas sila. Kaya kahit malalaki ang pakpak, kaya pa rin silang lumipad!
fact_en:
Why are birds so light?

Many bird bones are hollow with air spaces inside! This makes their bodies light, so their wings need less force to lift them. That's how even big birds with huge wings can still fly!

title: Ibon Flap vs Eroplano Still
fact_tl:
Bakit pumapagaspas ang ibon pero hindi ang eroplano?

Pareho silang gumagawa ng lift sa hugis. Pero pumapagaspas ang ibon para humila, habang naka-fixed ang pakpak ng eroplano at makina ang nagtutulak.
fact_en:
Why do birds flap but airplanes don't?

Both wings make lift from their shape. But birds flap to pull forward, while airplane wings stay fixed and engines push them.

title: Mahabang Lever Arm
fact_tl: Mas madaling magbuhat kapag mas mahaba ang lever arm sa kamay mo! Kaya may mahabang hawakan ang barreta para malayo ka sa fulcrum.
fact_en: Lifting is easier when the lever arm to your hand is longer! That's why a crowbar has a long handle to keep you far from the fulcrum.

title: Parehong Bilis Ibang Momentum
fact_tl: Sa parehong speed, mas malakas tumama ang mabigat na trak kaysa sa magaan na bisikleta! Ito ay dahil sa momentum, na nakadepende sa speed at mass, kaya mas mahirap pahintuin ang trak.
fact_en: At the same speed, a heavy truck hits much harder than a light bicycle! This is because of momentum, which depends on both speed and mass, making the heavier truck harder to stop.

title: Magkaibang Unit Parehong Bilis
fact_tl: Pwedeng gamitan ng iba't ibang units ang parehong speed! Halimbawa, ang 36 km/h ay katumbas ng 10 meters per second. Palaging tingnan ang units bago magkumpara para hindi magkamali.
fact_en: The same speed can use different units! For example, 36 km/h is exactly 10 meters per second. Always check the units before comparing speeds so you don't get the wrong answer.

title: Bilis Kotse Mahabang Preno
fact_tl: Kapag mas mabilis ang sasakyan, mas mahaba ang stopping distance! Kapag dinoble mo ang bilis, mas mahaba pa sa doble ang kailangan nitong layo para huminto. Kaya delikado ang sobrang bilis!
fact_en: The faster a car goes, the longer its stopping distance! If you double the speed, the stopping distance grows even more than double. That is why speeding is so dangerous!

title: Average Speed 240 km 4 Oras
fact_tl:
Paano natin malalaman ang average speed?

Hatiin lang ang layo sa oras! Kung maglalakbay ka ng 240 kilometers sa loob ng 4 na oras, ang average speed mo ay 60 km/h. Parang tuloy-tuloy kang bumibilis ng 60 km/h, kahit tumigil ka minsan!
fact_en:
How do we find average speed?

Divide total distance by total time! Traveling 240 kilometers in 4 hours gives an average speed of 60 km/h. It is like going steadily at 60 km/h, even if you stopped sometimes!

title: Fireworks Flash Muna Tunog
fact_tl:
Bakit nakikita natin ang fireworks bago marinig?

Dahil milyon-milyong beses na mas mabilis ang liwanag kaysa tunog! Nauuna ang flash sa iyong mga mata, at saka pa lang dumating ang mas mabagal na tunog. Kaya matatantya mo kung gaano kalayo ang paputok!
fact_en:
Why do we see fireworks before hearing them?

Light is millions of times faster than sound! The flash reaches your eyes first, and the slower sound reaches your ears later, helping you guess how far away the fireworks are!

title: Bilis Bus Kalsada Relative
fact_tl:
Gumagalaw ka ba ngayon?

Nakadepende! Sa loob ng bus, 0 ang bilis mo kumpara sa katabi mo, pero 60 km/h kumpara sa kalsada. Kahit nakaupo ka lang, umiikot ka nang mabilis kasabay ng Earth! Ang bilis ay laging relative.
fact_en:
Are you moving right now?

It depends! In a bus, your speed is 0 compared to your seatmate, but 60 km/h compared to the road. Even sitting still, you spin fast with the Earth! Speed is always relative.

title: Airspeed Ground Speed Tailwind
fact_tl:
Bakit mas matagal minsan ang return flights?

May airspeed at ground speed ang mga eroplano! Kapag may tailwind, mas mabilis ang ground speed kaya mas maaga kang dumarating. Kapag pasalunga sa hangin, mas mabagal. Kaya minsan mas matagal ang balikan!
fact_en:
Why do return flights sometimes take longer?

Airplanes have airspeed and ground speed! With a tailwind, ground speed is higher, so you arrive sooner. A headwind makes it slower, which is why a return trip can take longer!

title: Doble Bilis Enerhiya
fact_tl: Doblehin mo ang bilis, at ang kinetic energy ay magiging APAT na beses mas malaki—hindi lang doble! Dahil nakadepende ito sa bilis na nakakuwadrado. Kaya delikado ang overspeeding sa kalsada!
fact_en: Double your speed, and kinetic energy becomes FOUR times bigger—not just double! That's because it depends on speed squared. This is why speeding on roads is super dangerous!

title: Kinetic Energy Zero
fact_tl:
Puwede bang maging zero ang kinetic energy?

Oo! Kapag ganap na nakatigil ang isang bagay, zero ang kinetic energy nito. Pero hindi ito kayang maging negatibo—dahil ang pormula ay gumagamit ng bilis na nakakuwadrado, na laging zero o pataas!
fact_en:
Can kinetic energy ever be zero?

Yes! When an object is completely still, its kinetic energy is zero. But it can never be negative—because the formula uses speed squared, always zero or positive!

title: Lapad na Talim Sagwan Tubig
fact_tl: Ang lapad at patag na dulo ng sagwan ay nakakatulak ng mas maraming tubig sa bawat hila! Kung makitid ito, kaunti lang ang maaabot kaya mas mahina ang pasulong.
fact_en: The wide, flat end of a paddle pushes more water with each stroke! If the tip were narrow, it would grab less water and give a much weaker forward push.

title: Catch Pull Recovery Sagwan
fact_tl: Ang isang sagwan ay may tatlong bahagi: isawsaw sa tubig (catch), hilain pabalik (pull), at iaangat at ibalik sa unahan (recovery). Ulitin ito para tuloy-tuloy ang galaw!
fact_en: A paddle stroke has three parts: dip the blade in the water (catch), pull it back (pull), and lift it forward to repeat (recovery). Repeat this to keep moving!

title: Tahimik na Pagsagwan
fact_tl:
Bakit gumagamit ang mangingisda ng sagwan sa halip na makina?

Tahimik ang sagwan at hindi natatakot ang mga isda! Dahan-dahang nagsasagwan ang mga mangingisda papalapit sa pamingwitan para hindi makagawa ng ingay.
fact_en:
Why do fishers use a paddle instead of a motor?

Paddles are quiet and won't scare the fish! Fishers paddle slowly toward their spot to avoid making a loud disturbance in the water.

title: Kalamnan Braso Likod Sagwan
fact_tl:
Saan galing ang lakas mo sa pagsagwan?

Ang iyong muscles—braso, likod, at balikat—ang gumagalaw! Galing sa pagkain ang enerhiyang ito, kaya napapagod ka kapag matagal na nagsasagwan.
fact_en:
Where does your paddling power come from?

Your muscles—arms, back, and shoulders—move the paddle! This energy comes from the food you ate, which is why you get tired after a long time.

title: Patag na Talikod Iwas Hadlang
fact_tl: Ikiniling ng mga sanay na tagasagwan nang patag ang dulo kapag ibinabalik ito! Para hindi humampas sa hangin o sumalpok sa tubig, nababawasan ang hadlang kaya hindi sila gaanong napapagod.
fact_en: Skilled paddlers tilt the paddle blade flat when swinging it forward! This stops it from slapping the wind or splashing water, reducing resistance so they tire less.

title: Tunog 340 m/s Hangin
fact_tl:
Gaano kabilis ang tunog sa hangin?

Naglalakbay ang tunog ng mga 340 metro kada segundo sa hangin! Halos isang katlo ng kilometro iyon sa isang segundo, parang mabagal kumpara sa liwanag.
fact_en:
How fast does sound travel in air?

Sound travels about 340 meters per second in air! That is almost a third of a kilometer in one second, which seems slow compared to light.

title: Sigaw Bulong Parehong Bilis
fact_tl:
Mas mabilis ba ang malakas na tunog kaysa mahina?

Hindi! Ang lakas (amplitude) ay hiwalay sa bilis ng wave. Parehong 340 m/s ang sigaw at bulong sa parehong hangin!
fact_en:
Does a loud sound travel faster than a soft one?

Nope! Loudness (amplitude) is separate from wave speed. A shout and a whisper both travel at the same 340 m/s in the same air!

title: Mainit Hangin Mabilis Tunog
fact_tl: Bahagyang mas mabilis ang tunog sa mas mainit na hangin! Kapag mainit, mas mabilis gumagalaw ang air molecules kaya mas mabilis nilang naipapasa ang wave.
fact_en: Sound travels a little faster in warmer air! When it is hot, air molecules move faster and pass the wave along more quickly.

title: Sonar Echo Layo Barko
fact_tl:
Paano sumusukat ng layo ang mga barko?

Gamit ang bilis ng tunog at echo! Sa pag-time kung gaano katagal bumalik ang tunog, ginagamit ng sonar sa barko para makuha ang layo.
fact_en:
How do ships measure distance underwater?

They use sound speed and echoes! By timing how long a sound takes to bounce back, ships use sonar to find the exact distance.

title: Wave Speed vs Particle Uugoy
fact_tl:
Itinutulak ba ng alon ang mga particle nang mabilis?

Hindi! Iba ang wave speed. Mabilis dumaan ang alon, pero ang bawat particle ay umuugoy lang pataas-pababa sa isang lugar. Magkaiba sila!
fact_en:
Does a wave push particles forward really fast?

Nope! Wave speed is different. The wave passes by quickly, but each particle just wobbles up and down in its own spot. They are totally different!

title: Higpit Kuwerdas Wave Speed
fact_tl:
Bakit tumataas ang tono kapag hinihigpitan ang kuwerdas ng gitara?

Dahil mas mabilis lumakbay ang alon! Kapag mas mahigpit ang hila, tumataas ang wave speed, kaya mas mataas ang tonong naririnig mo.
fact_en:
Why does tightening a guitar string raise its pitch?

Because the wave travels faster! When you pull a guitar string tighter, the wave speed increases, which helps set the higher note you hear.

title: Tunog Walang Bilis Kalawakan
fact_tl: Tahimik ang outer space! Walang hangin o medium, kaya walang bilis ang tunog at hindi makakalat. Liwanag lang ang nakakadaan sa walang laman na espasyo.
fact_en: Outer space is totally silent! With no air or medium, sound has no speed and cannot spread. Only light can travel through empty space.

title: Taas Hindi Katumbas ng Bilis
fact_tl: Hindi laging mas mabilis ang malalaking alon ng dagat! Ang taas (amplitude) ay hiwalay sa bilis. Ang lalim ng tubig at ilalim ng dagat ang nagtatakda ng bilis, hindi ang laki.
fact_en: Bigger sea waves aren't always faster! A wave's height (amplitude) is separate from its speed. Water depth and the seafloor actually set the speed, not the size.

title: Momentum Trak Bisikleta
fact_tl:
Bakit mas mahirap pahintuin ang mabilis na trak kaysa mabagal na bisikleta?

Dahil sa momentum! Ito yung lakas ng galaw ng bagay, nakadepende sa mass at bilis. Mas mahirap pahintuin ang mabigat at mabilis, kaya mas mapanganib!
fact_en:
Ever wonder why a fast truck is harder to stop than a slow bike?

That's momentum! It's the strength of an object's motion, depending on its mass and speed. Heavy, fast things are harder to stop and more dangerous!

title: Friction Tulong Init
fact_tl: Kapaki-pakinabang ang friction sa grip ng sapatos at preno, pero nakakaubos ng gamit at gumagawa ng init! Nababawasan ito gamit ang langis o gulong, nadadagdagan gamit ang magaspang na ibabaw.
fact_en: Friction is useful for shoe grip and car brakes, but it wears things out and makes heat! We reduce it with oil or wheels, and increase it with rough surfaces.

title: Generator Power Plant
fact_tl: Karamihan ng kuryente ay ginagawa sa power plant gamit ang generator! Pinapaikot ang turbine gamit ang singaw, tubig, o hangin, na gumagawa ng electrical energy na dumadaloy sa wire sa atong bahay.
fact_en: Most electricity is made in a power plant using a generator! A turbine is spun by steam, water, or wind, producing electrical energy that flows through wires right to our homes.

title: Pakpak Lift Eroplano
fact_tl:
Paano ba lumilipad ang mga ibon at eroplano?

Lumilipad sila dahil sa hugis ng kanilang pakpak! Mas mabilis dumaloy ang hangin sa ibabaw ng pakpak kaysa sa ilalim, na lumilikha ng lift na nagtataas sa kanila.
fact_en:
How do birds and planes actually fly?

They fly because of their wing shape! Air flows faster over the top of the wing than underneath, creating lift that pushes them up into the sky.

title: Katig ng Bangka
fact_tl:
Paano hindi natatumba ang banca kahit may alon?

May katig sa magkabilang gilid na lumulutang sa tubig, na pumipigil sa makitid na bangka na tumba kahit may alon!
fact_en:
How does a banca stay from tipping over in the waves?

A banca has outriggers, or katig, floating on each side that keep the narrow boat from tipping over, even in waves!

title: Lever Hindi Gumawa Extra Energy
fact_tl:
Nagbibigay ba ang lever ng libreng lakas?

Hindi, hindi ito gumagawa ng dagdag na enerhiya! Para mas magaan ang pagbuhat, kailangan mong itulak ang dulo sa mas malayong distansya. May kapalit ang ginhawa!
fact_en:
Does a lever give you free strength?

Nope, it doesn't create extra energy! To make lifting easier, you must push your end through a longer distance. The easiness has a trade-off!

title: Lever ng Martilyo
fact_tl:
Paano nakabubunot ng pako ang martilyo?

Ang kuko ng martilyo ay isang lever! Ang nakadikit sa kahoy ang fulcrum, at ang paghila sa hawakan ang effort na madaling nakakabunot ng pako.
fact_en:
How does a hammer pull out nails?

The hammer's claw is a lever! The part on the wood is the fulcrum, and pulling the handle is the effort that easily yanks the nail out.

title: Lever Bar Stiff Hindi Goma Lubid
fact_tl: Kailangang matigas ang bara ng lever, hindi malambot! Babaluktot lang ang goma o lubid. Ang matigas na bara ang naglilipat ng lakas mo para maitaas ang bigat.
fact_en: A lever's bar must be stiff, not floppy! Rubber or rope just bends. A stiff bar carries your force straight from one end to the other to lift the weight.

title: Yuko Mababa Munti Kidlat Bukid
fact_tl: Kung mahuli ka ng kidlat sa bukid, yumuko ka at gawing maliit ang katawan mo! Ang pinakamataas na bagay ang pinakamadalas tamaan.
fact_en: If lightning catches you in an open field, crouch down low and make yourself small! The tallest thing around is most likely to get struck.

title: Kidlat Tumama Mataas na Bagay
fact_tl:
Bakit ang pinakamataas na bagay ang tinitirhan ng kidlat?

Pinapili ng kidlat ang pinakamalapit na daan mula sa ulap! Kaya mas delikado ang matayog—yumuko ka sa bukid!
fact_en:
Why does lightning hit the tallest thing around?

Lightning takes the shortest path from the cloud! The taller something is, the closer it gets to the cloud—so stay low in open areas!

title: 30-30 na Panuntunan
fact_tl:
Ano ang '30-30 rule' para sa kaligtasan sa kidlat?

Bilangin ang segundo pagkatapos ng kidlat at kulog! Kung wala pang 30 segundo, pumasok NA! Maghintay ng 30 minuto pagkatapos ng huling kulog bago lumabas.
fact_en:
What's the '30-30 rule' for lightning safety?

Count the seconds between flash and thunder! If it's under 30 seconds, go inside NOW! Then wait 30 minutes after the last thunder before going out.

title: Kotse Metal Kidlat Ligtas
fact_tl: Ang saradong metal na sasakyan ay ligtas na silungan! Ang metal shell ay nagdadala ng kuryente sa labas papunta sa lupa—hindi sa'yo sa loob!
fact_en: A closed metal car is a safe lightning hideout! The metal shell guides electricity around the outside to the ground—not through you inside!

title: Kotse Metal Body Hindi Goma
fact_tl:
Bakit ligtas ang sasakyan habang may kidlat?

Hindi ang gomang gulong—ang metal na katawan! Napakalakas ng kidlat para sa manipis na goma. Ang metal shell ay nagdadala ng kuryente palibot sa'yo!
fact_en:
Why is a car safe during lightning?

Not the rubber tires—the metal body! Lightning is too powerful for thin rubber. The metal shell channels electricity around you to the ground!

title: Unplug TV Appliances Kulog Bagyo
fact_tl:
Dapat bang kalasin ang TV kapag may bagyo at kidlat?

Oo! Kung tamaan ng kidlat ang power line, dadaloy ang sobrang lakas ng kuryente sa mga kable at masisira ang gamit. Kalasin para ligtas!
fact_en:
Should you unplug the TV during a lightning storm?

Yes! If lightning hits a power line, a huge surge of electricity can travel through wires and fry your appliances. Unplug them to stay safe!

title: Kidlat Telepono Shower Ayos
fact_tl: Kahit nasa bahay ka, iwasan ang teleponong may kable at pagligo habang may kidlat! Ang kuryente ay pwedeng dumaan sa metal na tubo at kable papunta sa'yo!
fact_en: Even inside your house, skip the corded phone and shower during lightning! Electricity can travel through metal pipes and wires straight to you!

title: Grupo Kalat Kalayo Kidlat Labas
fact_tl:
Ano ang dapat gawin ng grupo kung naabutan ng kidlat sa labas na walang silungan?

Maghiwa-hiwalay nang kaunti! Para kung may tumama, hindi lahat masaktan nang sabay-sabay.
fact_en:
What should a group do if caught outside in a lightning storm with no shelter?

Spread out a little! This way, if lightning strikes, not everyone gets hurt at the same time.

title: Kidlat Ulap Lupa Daloy
fact_tl: Ang kidlat ay malakas na daloy ng kuryente mula ulap papalupa! Iwasan ang pagiging daanan nito: huwag maging pinakamataas o humawak ng metal na nakadikit sa lupa.
fact_en: Lightning is a powerful flow of electricity from clouds to the ground! Don't be its easy path: avoid being the tallest thing or holding metal touching the ground.

title: Loob Gusali Ligtas Kidlat Bagyo
fact_tl:
Ano ang pinakaligtas na lugar kapag may bagyo at kidlat?

Pumasok sa loob ng matibay na gusali o bahay! Ang pader at bubong nito ay magpoprotekta sa iyo.
fact_en:
What is the safest place to be during a lightning storm?

Go inside a sturdy building or house! Its strong walls and roof will protect you from the lightning.

title: PH Kidlat Habagat Season
fact_tl: Sa Pilipinas, mas madalas ang kidlat tuwing tag-ulan at panahon ng bagyo, lalo na kapag habagat! Mag-ingat palagi at makinig sa babala ng PAGASA sa mga buwang ito.
fact_en: In the Philippines, lightning is more frequent during the rainy and typhoon season, especially the habagat! Always be careful and listen to PAGASA warnings during these months.

title: Buhok Tumayo Kidlat Babala
fact_tl: Kung biglang tumayo ang buhok mo at parang may kumikiliti sa balat habang may bagyo, malapit nang tumama ang kidlat! Dalian mong yumuko at gawing maliit ang iyong katawan.
fact_en: If your hair suddenly stands up and your skin tingles during a storm, a lightning strike is about to happen nearby! Crouch low and make yourself small right away.
